messages.subject: Unwanted R code echo in PDF
messages.subject_clean: Unwanted R code echo in PDF
messages.body_plain:
I'm converting a .Rnw file to a .tex file using knitr, and then converting to PDF. I have set echo = FALSE, but I'm still getting R code appearing in the PDF.

On the first few compiles, there is no R code in the PDF. Then after a few compiles, the source R code appears in a couple of sections at the top of the PDF. Then after more compiles, my entire source R code appears in the PDF.

Any suggestions as to the cause of the R code echoing in the PDF?

messages.subject: Creating a pdf with relative links to plots
messages.subject_clean: Creating a pdf with relative links to plots
messages.body_plain:
I'm trying to create a pdf document using knitr (& Rstudio) that will include hyperlinks to plots.

The links work with absolute addresses but fail with the error "The link 'file://./XXXXXX.pdf”  cannot be opened because the destination file cannot be found.' (From OSX Preview PDF viewer) when I try a relative address.

Any pointers to where I'm going wrong greatly appreciated.

Small example appended.

Thanks

Ian

---
title: "hyperlink_test"
author: "Ian Handel"
date: "16 June 2015"
output: pdf_document
---

```{r, echo = FALSE, results='asis'}
library(knitr)

link <- "histogram.pdf"

pdf((link), height = 6, width = 6)
hist(rnorm(1000))
dev.off()

kable(data.frame(link = paste0("file://./", link)))
```

messages.subject: Enforce PDF package vignette with knitr
messages.subject_clean: Enforce PDF package vignette with knitr
messages.body_plain:
I have a vignette for my package which compiles to a nice PDF when compiled with Rscript -e 'rmarkdown::render("tmod.rmd")'. When I compile and install the package, start R and type vignette("mypackagename"), a browser window opens with ugly looking HTML, without a title, without a table of contents and without references. Anyway, I don't want an HTML vignette; I want a PDF.

However, if I compile the vignette manually to pdf before creating the package, it shows up just fine.

What went wrong? Why is my PDF not generated automatically when I compile the package?

In the markdown file header, I have
---
title: "foo foo foo"
author: "Foofooary Finer"
date: "`r Sys.Date()`"
output:
  pdf_document:
vignette: >
  %\VignetteIndexEntry{FooFoo}
  %\VignetteKeyword{foo}
  %\VignetteEngine{knitr::knitr}
  %\SweaveUTF8
  \usepackage[utf8](inputenc)
abstract: |
  foo foo foo foo foo
toc: yes
bibliography: bibliography.bib
---

In the package DESCRIPTION file, I have
VignetteBuilder: knitr
Suggests: knitr

messages.body_plain:
You are right -- there isn't much documentation about it. There is a
help page ?knitr::vignette_engines, but it didn't explain what each
vignette engine does.

knitr::knitr uses R Markdown v1 to process .Rmd vignettes, and
knitr::rmarkdown uses R Markdown v2
(http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_migrating_from_v1.html).

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name

messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Enforce PDF package vignette with knitr
messages.body_plain:
> knitr::knitr uses R Markdown v1 to process .Rmd vignettes, and
> knitr::rmarkdown uses R Markdown v2
> (http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com/authoring_migrating_from_v1.html).

As an outsider -- someone who did not follow Sweave / knitr and who was just using old timey LaTeX until recently -- I think there is, for an uninformed user, a bit of a confusion around what is the document language (markdown, latex, latex/sweave, xml/html even), and what is the file output format (dvi, postscript, pdf, doc, html/css).

Here was how I understood the world:

1) there is "output" in the header. It clearly specifies what the output is supposed to be; pdf_document in this case.

2) there is this mysterious engine thing that either uses knitr::knitr or maybe knitr::rmarkdown.  Well, it is markdown in any case, isn't it? After all, I did specify the output as "pdf_document", didn't I? I should follow The Book, shouldn't I?

Also, rmarkdown can produce anything from a markdown file, so I did not see a connection between PDF output and using knitr::rmarkdown.

Do I understand the world correctly now -- the "output" option is honored only by knitr::rmarkdown, while knitr::knitr ignores it?

All the best,

j.

R Markdown v2. Almost everything you mentioned was specific to v2.
When you use R Markdown, chances are that you mean v2. I cannot wipe
out the history of Sweave, .Rnw/LaTeX, or R Markdown v1 in one day.
That is probably the source of confusion.

make it easier for future users to find answers and explanations:

messages.subject: a Ruby engine
messages.body_plain:
This html article : http://stla.github.io/stlapblog/posts/Ruby_is_cool.html
is generated by this Rmd : https://raw.githubusercontent.com/stla/stlapblog/gh-pages/posts/Ruby_is_cool.Rmd

The Rmd file includes a RUBY engine. The problem with the ruby engine currently implemented in knitr returns all the block code and then all the outputs: it does not split according to each time the code generates an output. My small RUBY engine is not intended to replace the one in knitr: it is far to be perfect !

The idea is, starting from a block code in a chunk like :

x=2
y=3
def f(a)
  w=a*a
  return w
end
puts f(x+y)
def g(a)
  return a*a*a
end

Then the RUBY engine will firstly generates this code and then send it to Ruby :

puts '>> x=2'
x=2
puts '>> y=3
y=3
puts '>> def f(a)
  w=a*a
  return w
end'
def f(a)
  w=a*a
  return w
end
puts '>> puts f(x+y)'
puts f(x+y)
puts '>> def g(a)
  return a*a*a
end'
def g(a)
  return a*a*a
end

Moreover there is an option memo to memorize the code in a chunk and an option use.memo to call the code in memory before running the current code.
It is far to be perfect but there many possible things to improve.

messages.subject: Created a shiny website with knitr
messages.subject_clean: Created a shiny website with knitr
messages.body_plain:
I was able to create a multi-page website using Rmd files and knitr. See https://github.com/vnijs/shiny-site. Works great ... mostly.

One thing that doesn't quite work the way I would like is rendering a slider. See example Rmd file linked below. sliderInput generates HTML but is rendered as a textinput in the html page. A work-around is to define the slider in server.R and use uiOutput in the Rmd file. Not a big deal. Just curious why it happens and if there is perhaps a better work-around.

https://github.com/vnijs/shiny-site/blob/master/page2.Rmd

Just in case ... I do know you can use the shiny runtime with rmarkdown to create an interactive webpage but, afaik, this doesn't allow you to build a multi-page website.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Created a shiny website with knitr
messages.subject_clean: [knitr] Created a shiny website with knitr
messages.body_plain:
My guess is that it is because you were using knitr::knit2html() (R
Markdown v1) to compile the Rmd documents, and R Markdown v1 does not
understand HTML dependencies. A slider is initially a text input, and
the JS library turns the text input into a slider. R Markdown v1 is
not aware of the JS dependency attached on sliderInput(), so the
slider is not rendered.

Regards,
Yihui
--
Yihui Xie <xiey...@gmail.com>
Web: http://yihui.name
